pictures.name: sheltering_boulder
pictures.scene: one great boulder standing alone on an open plain with a deep pocket of shade beneath its overhang, the dry ground at its foot lit warm and gold, the huge stone above rising dark against a pale sky

pictures.name: anger_gathering
pictures.scene: a wall of black storm cloud piled high over a flat empty land, a thin strip of fierce yellow light burning along the horizon beneath it at the bottom of the frame, the whole sky above heavy and closed

pictures.name: torrent_in_the_gorge
pictures.scene: brown floodwater tearing through a narrow rock gorge, its churned surface white and bright along the bottom of the frame, the wet walls above it rising sheer and dark until they lose all detail

pictures.name: stones_left_bare
pictures.scene: a wide bank of wet river stones left bare by fallen water, each stone lit warm and low by a sun near the horizon, the calmed river beyond them lying flat and dark and almost without any detail

pictures.name: torn_snare
pictures.scene: a snare net lying slack across the grass with a wide hole torn open through it, its cut cords lit bright along the bottom edge, the empty field beyond stretching away into evening shadow

pictures.name: heaven_and_earth_made
pictures.scene: a vast still land of low hills meeting an immense sky at a far horizon, the nearest grass and stone lit warm gold along the bottom of the frame, the whole depth of the sky above them dark and clear

lines.text: A song of ascents. Of David.
If the LORD had not been on our side—
if the LORD had not been on our side
when their anger flared against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive,
then the floods would have engulfed us,
then the torrent would have overwhelmed us,
who has not given us as prey to their teeth.
We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler;
the net is torn, and we have slipped away.
Our help is in the name of the LORD,
the Maker of heaven and earth.
